rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~87% 25bp / ~13% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Reuters); ECB Dec ~92%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~67%; BoC Dec ~34%; Deutsche Bank sees Fed hikes Dec, Jan, Mar
rows.read: Bets on faster Federal Reserve rate rises held overnight, keeping the dollar near its highest since April 2025. Hikes from Europe, Britain and Japan are expected too but already priced, so the gap keeps widening in the dollar's favour. Strong Japanese wholesale prices firmed the case for a Bank of Japan hike in December.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q (fcst +0.7%, Q2 +0.5%); Sep +0.2% m/m (fcst 0.0%), Aug revised to 0.0%; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd est. Fri 4:00 AM CT
rows.read: UK growth matched forecasts in the third quarter, solid enough to back the Bank of England's November hike but not enough to settle December. The US economy still looks firmer than Australia's, Canada's or New Zealand's, a split that favours the dollar. Euro-area growth figures on Friday are the next read.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Japan Oct wholesale prices +7.1% y/y (fcst 6.5%); US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%; US PPI Fri 7:30 AM CT fcst +0.4% m/m; Brent ~$91.6
rows.read: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's goal, which keeps the Fed hiking and supports the dollar. In Japan, the weak yen is pushing wholesale prices up fast, adding pressure on the Bank of Japan to raise rates. Oil's dip overnight eases the worry a little.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: Markets stayed calm overnight, so the safe-haven franc and yen drew little support. Talk of direct US–Iran talks eased some Gulf fears. A sudden flare-up in the Gulf is still the main thing that could change the mood fast.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$91.6 (−1.24%), WTI ~$85.5 (−1.2%) in Asia; Brent high ~$94.2 Wed; $116.72 at the Oct 30 close
rows.read: Oil gave back Wednesday's gains on reports that Vice President JD Vance may meet Iran's security chief. Cheaper oil helps energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area and takes some support from the Canadian dollar. Tanker attacks near Hormuz keep a floor under prices.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and the yen and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro. The dollar's rise has gone with most of those bets, though the large bet on the yen is losing money as it weakens. The next weekly report is due Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year ~4.99% in early trading; 10-year auction Nov 10 at 5.020%, bid-to-cover 2.46 (avg 2.60); $25B 30-year auction Thu 12:00 PM CT
rows.read: Weak demand at US government bond sales this week pushed long-term borrowing costs up, as buyers asked for more pay to hold US debt. That supports the dollar for now but is a worry if it spreads. A 30-year bond sale on Thursday is the next check.
